gpt.text:
Run the three “Next Commands” in order; they’re designed to (1) search/tune modules, (2) evaluate system-level candidates, then (3) generate a targeted fix plan based on what just happened.

## 1) Module-level autopilot (pick best module candidate)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --run --select-best
```
What this does:
- Runs module experiments defined in `module_registry.yaml`
- Compares results against your current champion (`baseline/champion_v5_latest.json`)
- If any candidate beats the champion per your selection criteria, it will mark/select it (implementation-dependent: often updates a “current best” pointer or writes a new artifact)

What to look for after it finishes:
- A summary table of candidates and their metrics (especially the same metrics you listed: `tuning_mean/min`, `lockbox_mean/min`)
- Confirmation of what it selected (or “no improvement found”)

## 2) System-level autopilot (evaluate full system candidates)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml --run
```
What this does:
- Runs end-to-end/system candidates listed in `system_candidates.yaml`
- Produces comparable metrics (typically tuning + lockbox) so you can see whether improvements generalize

What to look for:
- Any candidate that improves *lockbox_mean* (your more “real” generalization signal) without tanking lockbox_min
- Whether any system candidate is now a PASS and should be promoted (your handoff shows there were no PASS candidates last time)

## 3) Generate the “next fix” plan
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
What this does:
- Writes a markdown report with recommended next actions based on recent results + registry metadata
- Useful when you got “no PASS” and need directed debugging/tuning steps

Open the report afterward:
```bash
sed -n '1,200p' baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```

---

## How to decide what to do after these runs
- **If `aub_autopilot` selects a new best module**: re-run the system autopilot (step 2) to confirm lockbox gains.
- **If system autopilot finds a new PASS**: promote it (whatever your project’s promotion mechanism is—often copying/updating the champion JSON).
- **If nothing passes**: use `next_fix.md` to choose the next targeted change (often improving worst-case `*_min` or addressing a specific failure cluster).

If you paste the stdout summaries (or the resulting tables/paths to produced JSON reports), I can help interpret which candidate to promote and what the next fix should focus on (tuning vs lockbox, mean vs min).
